subject: Playbook proposal: model selection checks & rollback steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Green <maya@stratacloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Playbook proposal: model selection checks & rollback steps

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the product demo today — great context on your ingestion patterns and the short, high-variance prompts your support agents submit. Per our discussion, I put together a short playbook for next steps: model recommendations, a lightweight benchmark you can run, and immediate mitigations in case you observe quality regressions after a model update.

High-level recommendations (short):
- Candidate models: llama-2-13b-q4 (low-latency), redwood-7b-qa (higher quality for short context)
- Suggested prompt set: attached prompt_set_initial.json (50 representative examples from your sandbox)
- Quick benchmark: run the attached CSV against both models; focus on exact-match and false-positive rates for slot extraction. Link to benchmark harness: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-demo-benchmarks
- Safety net: pin the serving version during your initial trial; rollback checklist attached if you see a >7% degradation in matched intent.

Attachments: stratacloud_eval_results_v1.csv (example output), prompt_set_initial.json, rollback_checklist.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) You run the quick benchmark in your staging environment this week (I put the harness link above).
2) We schedule a 30-minute results review on Thursday to decide which model to promote to pilot.
3) If you see any regression, we can pin the previous model and trigger a fast rollback — details in rollback_checklist.pdf.

If you want, Karthik can outline the pin/rollback API calls and an emergency-runbook for your SRE.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear notes and attachments. A couple of immediate questions from our side after a quick skim:

1) We recently saw a small quality dip when Redwood rolled the 7b variant last month for another customer. Does your pin/rollback flow give us a guaranteed fast fallback (<15 minutes to restore baseline) if the new variant introduces downstream slot errors?
2) Can you confirm whether the candidate models you listed are already quantized on your hosted infra or whether we'd need a dedicated pool to hit our latency targets?

I'll kick off the benchmark against the prompt set today and loop in Carlos (tech lead) for any infra questions. We also need a short note for procurement detailing how pinning affects billing and SLA scope.

—Maya
Maya Green
Head of Product, StrataCloud

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Green <maya@stratacloud.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Playbook proposal: model selection checks & rollback steps

Hi Maya —

Quick answers to your questions and a proposed ops plan:

1) Rollback SLA: On hosted Redwood API, pinning to a previous model snapshot is normally immediate (API-level routing change) and takes effect in under a minute for new requests. Restoring in-flight throughput and any warmed KV caches can take longer; our runbook estimates 10–12 minutes to fully restore steady-state latency on the same fleet. I've attached a short rollback_checklist.pdf with the step-by-step and the API calls you can use (also described below).

2) Quantization & latency: Both candidate variants are available in quantized Q4 format on hosted infra. For your p95 latency target of <220ms, the 13b-q4 should be fine for short prompts; the redwood-7b-qa is slightly faster at lower cost but trades some recall. If you need guaranteed p95 at scale we can discuss a Dedicated pool with reserved capacity.

Proposed emergency runbook (summary):
- Alert triggers: >7% drop in slot extraction exact-match OR >3x increase in "fallback to handoff" rate
- Immediate action (within 5 mins): pin traffic to previous snapshot via /v1/serving/pin (payload example attached in rollback_checklist.pdf)
- Follow-up (5–15 mins): rerun the benchmark harness, inspect KV cache warmup, confirm latency targets; escalate to Redwood SRE if cold-starts exceed 12 mins

I've attached a small test artifact (stratacloud_eval_results_v1.csv) showing baseline differences we observed during a similar pilot. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the API commands — Jordan, want me to own the tech walkthrough on Thursday?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Plan for Thursday: 30-minute session (results + runbook). Proposed time: Thu 3/4 10:00 AM PST. Agenda: 1) benchmark readout (Maya/Carlos), 2) Karthik runs through the pin/rollback demo, 3) decide pilot model + billing implications for pin window. I'll send a calendar invite and include the attachment pack.

Procurement note (brief) for your team: pinning is a routing/serve-time control and does not create incremental model licensing charges beyond the underlying token usage. If you opt for Dedicated reserved capacity to guarantee latency, that is a separate commitment (monthly). I'll include a short bulletized note in the invite.

Jordan
